steps.title: Versatile
steps.body: Dry Riesling suits fish, shellfish, pork, sushi and Alsace's choucroute. Off-dry Riesling suits spicy Asian food: Thai, Sichuan, Indian; its sugar and low alcohol calm chilli. Sweet Riesling suits fruit desserts, blue cheese and foie gras. Riesling's acidity cuts fat and salt.

steps.title: Service
steps.body: Serve Riesling at 7 to 10 degrees; aged and sweet styles a little warmer, 10 to 12. Use a white wine glass with a narrowing rim to focus the aromas. Riesling under screw cap ages well and avoids cork taint.

steps.prompt: Why does off-dry Riesling suit spicy food?
options: Its sugar and low alcohol calm chilli heat
steps.explanation: Sweetness soothes, and low alcohol doesn't amplify the burn.

steps.body: Mosel Kabinett with a spicy Thai salad is one of the great wine and food matches. The wine's lime and sweetness echo the dish.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Dry Riesling suits fish, pork and choucroute
Off-dry Riesling is a top match for spicy food
Serve at 7 to 10 degrees in a narrowing glass
